evaluation.human_evals: The developer states that the model is only slightly less capable than the original, implying no formal human evaluation was reported.
evaluation.results_summary: The developer reports that the abliterated model performs close to the original, with only a slight drop in capability.

possible_risks.description: Lack of model transparency is due to insufficient documentation of the model design, development, and evaluation process and the absence of insights into the inner workings of the model.
possible_risks.justification: open-weight checkpoint card reports no training data, no safety evaluation, and no formal human evaluation; only a developer claim of slight capability drop

possible_risks.description: Hallucinations generate factually inaccurate or untruthful content relative to the model's training data or input. Hallucinations are also sometimes referred to lack of faithfulness or lack of groundedness. In some instances, synthetic data that is generated by large language models might include hallucinations that result in the data possibly being inaccurate, fabricated, or disconnected from reality. Hallucinations can compromise model performance, accuracy, and relevance.
possible_risks.justification: text-generation model with no reported factual grounding or evaluation; abliterated variant likely removes safety fine-tuning, increasing ungrounded or fabricated output risk

possible_risks.description: A model might generate language that leads to physical harm.  The language might include overtly violent, covertly dangerous, or otherwise indirectly unsafe statements.
possible_risks.justification: abliterated model is open-weight and likely has safety refusal training removed; card reports no safety evaluation, so harmful language risk is plausible

possible_risks.description: In AI-assisted decision-making tasks, reliance measures how much a person trusts (and potentially acts on) a model's output. Over-reliance occurs when a person puts too much trust in a model, accepting a model's output when the model's output is likely incorrect. Under-reliance is the opposite, where the person doesn't trust the model but should.
possible_risks.justification: developer claims only slight capability drop with no formal human evaluation, so users may over-trust outputs of a less capable abliterated model
